rh.identifiability_disclosure.no_overcla.reason: The paper does not claim cone specificity. M2 vs best M3 is -92.5 [-406.5,61.8], reported as not established. Verdict (b) 'No' is explicitly defined as 'no evidence that the nonlinearity sits on the cone axes', not evidence for another basis. The 'earned, scoped null' is framed as non-identifiability of where the compression sits, and its limits are fully disclosed and consistent with the logs: per-cone rho CIs span [0,1]; the L-vs-M split is detected in 12% of designed-M2 synthetic sets; coarse C2>M1 is detected in 2% at the fitted size; real CIs are 2.9-8.4x wider than synthetic; at real-data precision fitted-M2 effects exceed the real half-width in 0% of cases; an isotropic cone truth wins the panel test in 53%. The conclusion attributes the null to design and heterogeneity limits. Whether this null meets the task's 'earned' standard is a direction-side scientific judgment. Under the node's own carve-out, low power alone is a scientific weakness, and here it is disclosed rather than contradicted.
